author: Wes
text:
1.) At point 1 price engulfs a LFL - which at that point is PA (an
engulf which didn’t hit its target (2) So, we will now look for an
opportunity to short at the UFL.

2.) At point 1 price engulfs a LFL, retraces just a little bit and hits
its target (2) straight after – which means a new UFL (3) is formed. I
think this is what dengaima means – for an engulf to be tradeable we
need the engulf to not hit its target. (However, price failed to pick up
 the orders in the UFL (4) so I guess these will always be attractive
for the ITs?)

3.) In the 3rd scenario we have an engulf of the LFL (2) at (5) – so
again we look for a short opportunity at the UFL (3) But we have to be
more careful with this UFL. Why is that? That is because we have left
unfilled orders at the UFL (4). (UFL (3) is of course tradeable if you
like, but you should look for LTF PA to get the confirmation for the
trade (PA in a lower scale in yellow box)

Could this be the structure for a BSZ?
